findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Rollback = revert the commit. — It is not a rollback. shared/scripts does not auto-sync to the plugin cache and no reverse step was named. Revert WITHOUT re-sync leaves runtime and repo disagreeing about a git-tracked artifact with no detector, because the only corpus check is itself deleted by the revert. Revert WITH re-sync makes every record written in the window permanently unreadable, offering exactly the two exits this artifact forbids: repair or delete. Reverting also DELETES this run's own reviews.json - the file _committed_check exists to guarantee cannot vanish. RESOLVED: the section was rewritten. The supported undo is FIX-FORWARD - a new commit restoring the old vocabulary while KEEPING the read path, then update-marketplace.sh, then check_plugin_cache_sync.py --strict. Both failed revert branches are documented so nobody re-derives them.

Claim under doubt: That window is bounded by the PR not being auto-merged and by the revert being a same-day operation. — That is an assumption about the operator, not a property of the system. Not arming auto-merge bounds WHEN the merge happens; it bounds nothing about how many records the new producer writes afterwards. No counter, no ceiling, no detector. RESOLVED: replaced with the actual bound - every iterate run between the cache sync and any undo - and labelled a residual rather than a mitigation.

Claim under doubt: Preserving a legacy gates row is inert, not ambiguous, because entry_for's precedence makes the reviews row authoritative. — True in the producer, false in the only consumer the change exists to serve. unreadPassCount walks every record-level key outside KNOWN_RECORD_KEYS and counts any value carrying a review_type, so a record with BOTH reviews.spec and gates.spec renders the spec row AND appends 'this run also recorded 1 review pass somewhere this version does not read'. It tells the reader a pass is missing from the list it just showed them. Reachable in the rollout window via a record init'ed by the old plugin cache. RESOLVED IN CODE, not merely documented: upsert_review now drops a still-PENDING legacy row once the real answer is written (new lib/review_record_legacy.py::drop_unanswered_legacy). Pending is the absence of an answer, so nothing is destroyed; a TERMINAL legacy row is never touched. Two new tests pin both directions.

Claim under doubt: reviews stays strict because strictness protects the cross-repo mirror. — The mirror stopped rejecting strangers - that is the entire premise of this iterate. The sentence was reworded but the inference under it was never re-derived, so the change repeals the reason and keeps the conclusion. Consequence: the producer is now the strictest reader of its own format, and every future REVIEW_TYPES growth needs the same transitional read path, because old and new plugin caches coexist by design. LEGACY_GATE_TYPES is a name-keyed exemption for one key, not a mechanism. PARTIALLY RESOLVED, deliberately: the false justification is deleted and replaced with the one that holds - the consumer DISPLAYS so guessing costs a wrong row, this gate BLOCKS DELIVERY so guessing costs a wrong verdict. The recurring cost is stated in the spec under 'The strictness we kept, and what it costs' instead of hidden, and the relax-unknown alternative is FILED as triage trg-ee440345. Changing a fail-closed validator after three review stages passed on the current design belongs in its own iterate.

Claim under doubt: AC10 discharges the deployment risk. — Three problems. (a) It is discharged by prose and checked by nobody - the external review raised exactly this and returned 'revise'. (b) The two preconditions are not interchangeable and were listed as a set: the cache sync must FOLLOW the merge because it turns the producer on, while the webui redeploy must PRECEDE the existence of the first new-shape record. (c) That record already exists pre-merge - this run's own reviews.json is in the worktree, and the webui resolves live-run artifacts from the registered worktree, so framing the redeploy as a MERGE precondition is late by one commit. RESOLVED: AC10 is now an ordered four-step table with a named verification for each - re-run the 536-file marker grep for the redeploy, paste check_plugin_cache_sync.py --strict output for the cache sync. The pre-merge exposure is stated and was CHECKED: this worktree does not appear in the webui's projects.json or sdk-sessions.json, so it is not observable here, though it would be for a tracked run.

Claim under doubt: AC9 swept every place that describes the retired contract as current. — A fourth stale docstring survives, in a file the diff does not touch: it asserts the consumer 'rejects an unknown key AND a bumped schema_version' as present tense. Both of its assertions survive the rewrite, so nothing goes red - which is exactly why it was missed. RESOLVED: the docstring now says the contract is looser, not gone - the two guards were lifted in ce21323e, and what did NOT change is that an invalid record still renders as a data-integrity fault rather than falling back to the markers, which is why the test still exists.

Claim under doubt: shipwright-webui origin/main is ce21323e. — The tip has moved to 01b25b17. The substantive claim holds, but the identifier a future reader will use to re-check the mirror is wrong in four places. RESOLVED after re-verifying both facts - ce21323e is still an ancestor of origin/main and the tolerant reader is present at the current tip. The spec now names ce21323e as the commit that INTRODUCED the reader, not the branch tip.

Claim under doubt: A live run could reach a GREEN F11 with spec never answered, now that validate_record permanently tolerates its absence. — COULD NOT BREAK IT, and this is recorded because a failed attack is evidence. Attacked close-missing (targets come from pending_types, so spec is always in the batch), --force (upsert_review reads entry_for across BOTH sections before the immutability check), a hand-edited record with reviews.spec deleted (validate_record accepts it, but pending_types reports it pending and the gate blocks), a terminal gates.spec with no reviews.spec (passes, but it is a written, schema-validated, evidence-checked answer - identical in cost to fabricating reviews.spec, and the module already concedes it cannot defeat deliberate fabrication), and every early return in check_review_record. The tolerance genuinely buys reading and nothing else. The webui claim was also verified independently against the merged TypeScript rather than our summary: version floor, strangers rendered, pinned five still required, key regex, MAX_REVIEW_TYPES and MAX_KNOWN_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION all match the four mirror constants in our test.
